column1: # selftest-suite-timings.tsv — one row per suite whose measured cost is at or above the
# threshold below. Its one consumer is tools/run-selftests.sh, which defers every listed suite
# unless --full is passed (the milestone-3 lane runs without it, so the lane stays inside a turn).
# A row naming no discovered suite is a HARD ERROR (run-selftests.sh's stale-row posture). A
# suite ABSENT from this file is treated as fast. A row below the threshold is ignored at read
# time, so it has no reason to be here.
# THE DEFERRAL RULE SELECTS PURELY ON MEASURED DURATION (#780). It has no visibility into
# whether a suite is the sole producer or consumer of a shared-resource class, so a row here can
# defer every suite that would otherwise exercise that class on a milestone-3 lane — that is what
# happened to the pre-#780 fixture reaper, whose two producing suites were both deferred while a
# lane discovered them. The surviving instance of that blind spot is the
# tools/selftest-cache-inputs.tsv cache: two of its three declaring suites
# (milestone-gate-selftest.sh, check-lane-chain-selftest.sh) are deferred by this table, so a
# milestone-3 lane has exactly one cacheable suite (cost-block-selftest.sh) to actually exercise
